audit_status.source_base: Greek Acts text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Herod persecution, James killed, Peter imprisoned and angel-released, prayer house of Mary, Rhoda, Herod's death, word growth.

verses.restored: At that time Herod the king laid hands on some from the assembly to do harm.

familiar.text: Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church.

modern.text: About that time, King Herod reached out to harm some who belonged to the church.

original.text: Κατʼ ἐκεῖνον δὲ τὸν καιρὸν ἐπέβαλεν Ἡρῴδης ὁ βασιλεὺς τὰς χεῖρας κακῶσαί τινας τῶν ἀπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας.

verses.restored: He killed James the brother of John with a sword.

familiar.text: And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.

modern.text: He had James, the brother of John, put to death with the sword.

original.text: ἀνεῖλεν δὲ Ἰάκωβον τὸν ἀδελφὸν Ἰωάννου μαχαίρῃ.

verses.restored: Seeing that it was pleasing to the Judeans, he proceeded to arrest Peter also. These were the days of Unleavened Bread.

familiar.text: And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also. (Then were the days of unleavened bread.)

modern.text: And seeing that this pleased the Jews, Herod proceeded to seize Peter during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

original.text: ⸂ἰδὼν δὲ⸃ ὅτι ἀρεστόν ἐστιν τοῖς Ἰουδαίοις προσέθετο συλλαβεῖν καὶ Πέτρον (ἦσαν ⸀δὲ ἡμέραι τῶν ἀζύμων),

verses.restored: Seizing him, he put him in prison, handing him over to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending after the Passover to bring him up to the people.

familiar.text: And when he had apprehended him, he put him in prison, and delivered him to four quaternions of soldiers to keep him; intending after Easter to bring him forth to the people.

modern.text: He arrested him and put him in prison, handing him over to be guarded by four squads of four soldiers each. Herod intended to bring him out to the people after the Passover. The Rescue of Peter

original.text: ὃν καὶ πιάσας ἔθετο εἰς φυλακήν, παραδοὺς τέσσαρσιν τετραδίοις στρατιωτῶν φυλάσσειν αὐτόν, βουλόμενος μετὰ τὸ πάσχα ἀναγαγεῖν αὐτὸν τῷ λαῷ.

verses.restored: So Peter was being kept in the prison, but prayer was being made earnestly by the assembly to the Divine concerning him.

familiar.text: Peter therefore was kept in prison: but prayer was made without ceasing of the church unto God for him.

modern.text: So Peter was kept in prison, but the church was fervently praying to God for him.

original.text: ὁ μὲν οὖν Πέτρος ἐτηρεῖτο ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· προσευχὴ δὲ ἦν ⸀ἐκτενῶς γινομένη ὑπὸ τῆς ἐκκλησίας πρὸς τὸν θεὸν ⸀περὶ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: When Herod was about to bring him forward, that night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, and guards before the door were keeping the prison.

familiar.text: And when Herod would have brought him forth, the same night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains: and the keepers before the door kept the prison.

modern.text: On the night before Herod was to bring him to trial, Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, with sentries standing guard at the entrance to the prison.

original.text: Ὅτε δὲ ἤμελλεν ⸂προαγαγεῖν αὐτὸν⸃ ὁ Ἡρῴδης, τῇ νυκτὶ ἐκείνῃ ἦν ὁ Πέτρος κοιμώμενος μεταξὺ δύο στρατιωτῶν δεδεμένος ἁλύσεσιν δυσίν, φύλακές τε πρὸ τῆς θύρας ἐτήρουν τὴν φυλακήν.

verses.restored: Look, a messenger of the Lord stood by, and light shone in the cell. Striking Peter's side, he awakened him, saying, Rise quickly. And the chains fell from his hands.

familiar.text: And, behold, the angel of the Lord came upon him, and a light shined in the prison: and he smote Peter on the side, and raised him up, saying, Arise up quickly. And his chains fell off from his hands.

modern.text: Suddenly an angel of the Lord appeared and a light shone in the cell. He tapped Peter on the side and woke him up, saying, “Get up quickly.” And the chains fell off his wrists.

original.text: καὶ ἰδοὺ ἄγγελος κυρίου ἐπέστη, καὶ φῶς ἔλαμψεν ἐν τῷ οἰκήματι· πατάξας δὲ τὴν πλευρὰν τοῦ Πέτρου ἤγειρεν αὐτὸν λέγων· Ἀνάστα ἐν τάχει· καὶ ἐξέπεσαν αὐτοῦ αἱ ἁλύσεις ἐκ τῶν χειρῶν.

verses.restored: The messenger said to him, Belt yourself and tie on your sandals. He did so. And he says to him, Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.

familiar.text: And the angel said unto him, Gird thyself, and bind on thy sandals. And so he did. And he saith unto him, Cast thy garment about thee, and follow me.

modern.text: “Get dressed and put on your sandals,” said the angel. Peter did so, and the angel told him, “Wrap your cloak around you and follow me.”

original.text: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ ὁ ἄγγελος πρὸς αὐτόν· ⸀Ζῶσαι καὶ ὑπόδησαι τὰ σανδάλιά σου· ἐποίησεν δὲ οὕτως. καὶ λέγει αὐτῷ· Περιβαλοῦ τὸ ἱμάτιόν σου καὶ ἀκολούθει μοι.

verses.restored: Going out, he was following, and he did not know that what was happening through the messenger was real, but thought he was seeing a vision.

familiar.text: And he went out, and followed him; and wist not that it was true which was done by the angel; but thought he saw a vision.

modern.text: So Peter followed him out, but he was unaware that what the angel was doing was real. He thought he was only seeing a vision.

original.text: καὶ ἐξελθὼν ⸀ἠκολούθει, καὶ οὐκ ᾔδει ὅτι ἀληθές ἐστιν τὸ γινόμενον διὰ τοῦ ἀγγέλου, ἐδόκει δὲ ὅραμα βλέπειν.

verses.restored: Passing the first guard and the second, they came to the iron gate leading into the city, which opened to them by itself. Going out, they went forward one street, and immediately the messenger departed from him.

familiar.text: When they were past the first and the second ward, they came unto the iron gate that leadeth unto the city; which opened to them of his own accord: and they went out, and passed on through one street; and forthwith the angel departed from him.

modern.text: They passed the first and second guards and came to the iron gate leading to the city, which opened for them by itself. When they had gone outside and walked the length of one block, the angel suddenly left him.

original.text: διελθόντες δὲ πρώτην φυλακὴν καὶ δευτέραν ἦλθαν ἐπὶ τὴν πύλην τὴν σιδηρᾶν τὴν φέρουσαν εἰς τὴν πόλιν, ἥτις αὐτομάτη ἠνοίγη αὐτοῖς, καὶ ἐξελθόντες προῆλθον ῥύμην μίαν, καὶ εὐθέως ἀπέστη ὁ ἄγγελος ἀπʼ αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Peter, coming to himself, said, Now I know truly that the Lord sent his messenger and rescued me from Herod's hand and all the expectation of the Judean people.

familiar.text: And when Peter was come to himself, he said, Now I know of a surety, that the LORD hath sent his angel, and hath delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews.

modern.text: Then Peter came to himself and said, “Now I know for sure that the Lord has sent His angel and rescued me from Herod’s grasp and from everything the Jewish people were anticipating.”

original.text: καὶ ὁ Πέτρος ⸂ἐν ἑαυτῷ γενόμενος⸃ εἶπεν· Νῦν οἶδα ἀληθῶς ὅτι ἐξαπέστειλεν ⸀ὁ κύριος τὸν ἄγγελον αὐτοῦ καὶ ἐξείλατό με ἐκ χειρὸς Ἡρῴδου καὶ πάσης τῆς προσδοκίας τοῦ λαοῦ τῶν Ἰουδαίων.

verses.restored: Knowing this, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John called Mark, where many were gathered together and praying.

familiar.text: And when he had considered the thing, he came to the house of Mary the mother of John, whose surname was Mark; where many were gathered together praying.

modern.text: And when he had realized this, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, also called Mark, where many people had gathered together and were praying.

original.text: Συνιδών τε ἦλθεν ἐπὶ τὴν οἰκίαν ⸀τῆς Μαρίας τῆς μητρὸς Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐπικαλουμένου Μάρκου, οὗ ἦσαν ἱκανοὶ συνηθροισμένοι καὶ προσευχόμενοι.

verses.restored: When he knocked at the door of the gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.

familiar.text: And as Peter knocked at the door of the gate, a damsel came to hearken, named Rhoda.

modern.text: He knocked at the outer gate, and a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer it.

original.text: κρούσαντος δὲ ⸀αὐτοῦ τὴν θύραν τοῦ πυλῶνος προσῆλθε παιδίσκη ὑπακοῦσαι ὀνόματι Ῥόδη,

verses.restored: Recognizing Peter's voice, because of joy she did not open the gate, but running in, reported that Peter stood before the gate.

familiar.text: And when she knew Peter’s voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.

modern.text: When she recognized Peter’s voice, she was so overjoyed that she forgot to open the gate, but ran inside and announced, “Peter is standing at the gate!”

original.text: καὶ ἐπιγνοῦσα τὴν φωνὴν τοῦ Πέτρου ἀπὸ τῆς χαρᾶς οὐκ ἤνοιξεν τὸν πυλῶνα, εἰσδραμοῦσα δὲ ἀπήγγειλεν ἑστάναι τὸν Πέτρον πρὸ τοῦ πυλῶνος.

verses.restored: They said to her, You are mad. But she kept insisting it was so. They were saying, It is his messenger.

familiar.text: And they said unto her, Thou art mad. But she constantly affirmed that it was even so. Then said they, It is his angel.

modern.text: “You are out of your mind,” they told her. But when she kept insisting it was so, they said, “It must be his angel.”

original.text: οἱ δὲ πρὸς αὐτὴν εἶπαν· Μαίνῃ. ἡ δὲ διϊσχυρίζετο οὕτως ἔχειν. οἱ δὲ ἔλεγον· Ὁ ἄγγελός ⸂ἐστιν αὐτοῦ⸃.

verses.restored: But Peter continued knocking. Opening, they saw him and were amazed.

familiar.text: But Peter continued knocking: and when they had opened the door, and saw him, they were astonished.

modern.text: But Peter kept on knocking, and when they opened the door and saw him, they were astounded.

original.text: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος ἐπέμενεν κρούων· ἀνοίξαντες δὲ εἶδαν αὐτὸν καὶ ἐξέστησαν.

verses.restored: Motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he described to them how the Lord brought him out of the prison. He said, Report these things to James and to the siblings. And going out, he went to another place.

familiar.text: But he, beckoning unto them with the hand to hold their peace, declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren. And he departed, and went into another place.

modern.text: Peter motioned with his hand for silence, and he described how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. “Send word to James and to the brothers,” he said, and he left for another place.

original.text: κατασείσας δὲ αὐτοῖς τῇ χειρὶ σιγᾶν διηγήσατο αὐτοῖς πῶς ὁ κύριος αὐτὸν ἐξήγαγεν ἐκ τῆς φυλακῆς, εἶπέν ⸀τε· Ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰακώβῳ καὶ τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ταῦτα. καὶ ἐξελθὼν ἐπορεύθη εἰς ἕτερον τόπον.

verses.restored: When day came, there was no small disturbance among the soldiers over what had become of Peter.

familiar.text: Now as soon as it was day, there was no small stir among the soldiers, what was become of Peter.

modern.text: At daybreak there was no small commotion among the soldiers as to what had become of Peter.

original.text: Γενομένης δὲ ἡμέρας ἦν τάραχος οὐκ ὀλίγος ἐν τοῖς στρατιώταις, τί ἄρα ὁ Πέτρος ἐγένετο.

verses.restored: Herod, searching for him and not finding him, examined the guards and commanded them to be led away. Going down from Judea to Caesarea, he stayed there.

familiar.text: And when Herod had sought for him, and found him not, he examined the keepers, and commanded that they should be put to death. And he went down from Judaea to Caesarea, and there abode.

modern.text: After Herod had searched for him unsuccessfully, he examined the guards and ordered that they be executed. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and spent some time there. The Death of Herod

original.text: Ἡρῴδης δὲ ἐπιζητήσας αὐτὸν καὶ μὴ εὑρὼν ἀνακρίνας τοὺς φύλακας ἐκέλευσεν ἀπαχθῆναι, καὶ κατελθὼν ἀπὸ τῆς Ἰουδαίας ⸀εἰς Καισάρειαν διέτριβεν.

verses.restored: He was angrily disposed toward the Tyrians and Sidonians. They came to him with one accord, and persuading Blastus, the one over the king's bedchamber, they were asking for peace, because their country was fed from the king's country.

familiar.text: And Herod was highly displeased with them of Tyre and Sidon: but they came with one accord to him, and, having made Blastus the king’s chamberlain their friend, desired peace; because their country was nourished by the king’s country.

modern.text: Now Herod was in a furious dispute with the people of Tyre and Sidon, and they convened before him. Having secured the support of Blastus, the king’s chamberlain, they asked for peace, because their region depended on the king’s country for food.

original.text: Ἦν ⸀δὲ θυμομαχῶν Τυρίοις καὶ Σιδωνίοις· ὁμοθυμαδὸν δὲ παρῆσαν πρὸς αὐτόν, καὶ πείσαντες Βλάστον τὸν ἐπὶ τοῦ κοιτῶνος τοῦ βασιλέως ᾐτοῦντο εἰρήνην διὰ τὸ τρέφεσθαι αὐτῶν τὴν χώραν ἀπὸ τῆς βασιλικῆς.

verses.restored: On an appointed day Herod, putting on royal clothing and sitting on the judgment seat, was delivering a public address to them.

familiar.text: And upon a set day Herod, arrayed in royal apparel, sat upon his throne, and made an oration unto them.

modern.text: On the appointed day, Herod donned his royal robes, sat on his throne, and addressed the people.

original.text: τακτῇ δὲ ἡμέρᾳ ὁ Ἡρῴδης ἐνδυσάμενος ἐσθῆτα βασιλικὴν ⸀καὶ καθίσας ἐπὶ τοῦ βήματος ἐδημηγόρει πρὸς αὐτούς·

verses.restored: The people were crying out, A god's voice and not a human's.

familiar.text: And the people gave a shout, saying, It is the voice of a god, and not of a man.

modern.text: And they began to shout, “This is the voice of a god, not a man!”

original.text: ὁ δὲ δῆμος ἐπεφώνει· ⸂Θεοῦ φωνὴ⸃ καὶ οὐκ ἀνθρώπου.

verses.restored: Immediately a messenger of the Lord struck him because he did not give the glory to the Divine, and being eaten by worms, he breathed out.

familiar.text: And immediately the angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory: and he was eaten of worms, and gave up the ghost.

modern.text: Immediately, because Herod did not give glory to God, an angel of the Lord struck him down, and he was eaten by worms and died.

original.text: παραχρῆμα δὲ ἐπάταξεν αὐτὸν ἄγγελος κυρίου ἀνθʼ ὧν οὐκ ἔδωκεν ⸀τὴν δόξαν τῷ θεῷ, καὶ γενόμενος σκωληκόβρωτος ἐξέψυξεν.

verses.restored: But the word of the Divine grew and multiplied.

familiar.text: But the word of God grew and multiplied.

modern.text: But the word of God continued to spread and multiply.

original.text: Ὁ δὲ λόγος τοῦ ⸀θεοῦ ηὔξανεν καὶ ἐπληθύνετο.

verses.restored: Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, having fulfilled the service, taking along John who was called Mark.

familiar.text: And Barnabas and Saul returned from Jerusalem, when they had fulfilled their ministry, and took with them John, whose surname was Mark.

modern.text: When Barnabas and Saul had fulfilled their mission to Jerusalem, they returned, bringing with them John, also called Mark.

original.text: Βαρναβᾶς δὲ καὶ Σαῦλος ὑπέστρεψαν, ⸀εἰς Ἰερουσαλὴμ πληρώσαντες τὴν διακονίαν, ⸀συμπαραλαβόντες Ἰωάννην τὸν ἐπικληθέντα Μᾶρκον.
